title: Military encounters since 2019: USS Kidd, Oman, Yemen and USS Jackson
notes: Added: not in Appendix T. The post-2019 encounters the hearings and releases made public form their own group; they are neither Nimitz nor Roosevelt.

lead.text: Since 2019 US military encounters with unidentified objects have reached the record by several separate routes: Navy deck logs obtained under FOIA for the July 2019 swarms off California, an active-duty sailor's sworn account to Congress of USS Jackson in 2023, the Department's own release in August 2026 of files on a 2021 gunship encounter over the Gulf of Oman, and AARO's report of a mass event off Virginia.

summary.text: The group covers five events: the multi-night drone swarms around USS Kidd and other destroyers off Southern California in July 2019, recorded in deck logs; the AC-130J encounter over the Gulf of Oman on 8 September 2021; Alexandro Wiggins's account of four objects, one rising from the ocean, seen from USS Jackson in Warning Area W-291 on 15 February 2023; a video shown by Rep. Burlison said to show an MQ-9 firing a Hellfire at an orb off Yemen in October 2024; and the Navy report of about 100 objects off Virginia carried in AARO's FY2025 report.

Each reached the public by a different path, and the path is part of the story: FOIA for the 2019 deck logs, journalists and then a House task force for the Jackson footage, a hearing for the Yemen video, the Department's fifth release for the Gulf of Oman files, and AARO's own annual report for the Virginia event.
The board sets these beside the Nimitz case of 2004, in the same Southern California training space, which has a topic of its own.

record.text: USS Kidd's deck logs, obtained under FOIA, record UAVs first spotted around 2200 on 14 July 2019 and multiple UAVs around the ship by 2120 the next night. The logs also record a white light hovering over USS Rafael Peralta's flight deck for over 90 minutes while the ship made 16 knots in low visibility, and the cruise ship Carnival Imagination reporting five or six drones on 15 July.

Further incidents were logged on 25 and 30 July 2019; the Navy, Coast Guard and FBI investigated and the matter reached the Chief of Naval Operations. The deck logs of Kidd, Rafael Peralta, Russell and John Finn were cross-checked against AIS tracking, and, like the Nimitz case in the same training space, the 2019 events produced no attribution.

The printed record of the 9 September 2025 House hearing lists Chief Alexandro Wiggins, U.S. Navy, as a witness, and Rep. Burlison said from the dais that he was the first witness to come forward who was currently serving.

The Department's fifth release, dated 7 August 2026 on the war.gov portal, holds 41 files, 16 of them videos, among them DOW-UAP-PR122 and the intelligence report DOW-UAP-D101 on the AC-130J encounter over the Gulf of Oman on 8 September 2021.

AARO's FY2025 report, covering 2 June 2024 to 30 May 2025, records one maritime report from US Navy assets describing approximately 100 airborne UAP and two likely uncrewed surface systems off the coast of Virginia, under active investigation, and states that a lack of timely and actionable sensor data continues to constrain its ability to resolve cases.
AARO issued a Sources Sought Notice on SAM.gov for a custom case management system hosted on JWICS, with capabilities statements due 9 June 2025.

claimed.text: Wiggins, a Senior Chief aboard USS Jackson, says in his written statement that on 15 February 2023 at about 1915 PST in Warning Area W-291 he saw a light rising from the waterline, consistent with a platform emerging from the ocean, and that the self-luminous tic-tac object joined three similar objects with no visible control surfaces and no exhaust plume.
He says the four held controlled geometry and departed together with near-instantaneous acceleration and no sonic boom, and he testified that the object was detected on multiple radar systems.

By Wiggins's account, combat information center personnel recorded the event on the ship's Star SAFIRE multi-spectral EO/IR system and reported to the Tactical Action Officer, and the footage carries timestamps, latitude and longitude and platform readouts consistent with the ship's position.

How the Jackson account reached us: by Wiggins's statement, the video was published by the journalists Jeremy Corbell and George Knapp rather than released by the Navy or AARO, and he then testified about it as an active-duty sailor. He told the hearing that objects manoeuvring outside known profiles are first and foremost a safety issue.

DefenseScoop reported that at the 9 September 2025 hearing Rep. Burlison unveiled video of a US MQ-9 firing a Hellfire missile at a high-speed orb off Yemen in October 2024, and that the object appeared to be hit but not destroyed.

EarthSky's summary of the released Gulf of Oman files says six AC-130J videos and report DOW-UAP-D101 document about 25 instances of UAP, cold orbs about four feet across flying low at 250 to 1,300 mph, which reportedly reacted to the aircraft's cannon fire.

DefenseScoop reported on 21 July 2026 that AARO was investigating the Navy report of about 100 objects and two likely uncrewed surface systems off Virginia, the only maritime case among the 319 reports in the FY2025 report; AARO disclosed it the same day it published that report.

contested.text: AARO's FY2025 report states that none of the cases it resolved indicate advanced foreign adversarial capabilities or breakthrough technologies, and says a lack of timely and actionable sensor data continues to constrain its ability to resolve cases.
The same report says AARO received no reports indicating flight safety concerns in its period, while Wiggins told Congress that such encounters are first and foremost a safety issue.

On the board's reading, the Yemen shot and the Gulf of Oman engagement, with the MQ-9 lock in DOW-UAP-PR051, are weapons employments against objects that were not destroyed, and none is described as an engagement in any AARO annual report; the Gulf of Oman encounter falls inside the FY2023 and FY2024 reporting periods and appears in neither. This is inference from what the reports omit.

The Jackson footage, which Wiggins says carries time and position metadata, came to the public outside the official channel: it was published by journalists, and AARO's FY2025 report does not say whether the Jackson account is in its holdings, which the board records as an open inference.

The Virginia event has no public case number, incident date, hull or unit, and the Pentagon declined to give more; the board notes that AARO's purpose-built case system was still at the sources-sought stage in mid-2025. Both points are the board's inference from the reporting.

questions: Was the USS Jackson Star SAFIRE recording ever submitted to AARO, under what case number, and does it appear in the FY2023, FY2024 or FY2025 holdings?
Who were the other combat information center watchstanders aboard USS Jackson on 15 February 2023?
What unit flew the MQ-9 off Yemen, what is the video's chain of custody, who authorised its showing, and has the Department confirmed it?
Why does neither the FY2023 nor the FY2024 AARO report describe the Gulf of Oman gunship encounter?
When did the Virginia event happen, which ships or squadrons reported it, and what case number does it carry?
Who operated the aircraft that swarmed the destroyers off California in July 2019?
